title: Another Person making a game with AI.
author: FrostyBuildsGames
selftext:
Hello everyone ! 

I've never created a game before. I always wanted to.. but I never had the time. Now with the help of AI, it feels possible, so I wanted to recreate a childhood game that I played a lot as a kid. I used to have Super Mario Advance 2 on my Game Boy Advance and I played so many hours of a mode called Mario Bros. Classic. Honestly, I played that mode more than Super Mario World itself.

So now I'm trying to create a game similar to that! 😄 It's a single screen platformer made in Godot. Enemies walk along the platforms. You hit them from below to flip them over, then kick them off before they get back up. Clear every enemy to finish the wave.

The  video show the very first version, so it's all coloured rectangles. No art yet. I wanted it to feel right to play before making it look good. 

Stack im using : 

* **Engine:** Godot 4 (GDScript)
* **Code:** Claude Code in VS Code.
* **Second AI:** Codex, for planning, reviewing and concept art

  
I have zero coding or art background so the AI does the heavy lifting and I make the decisions how the game should feel.. what the enemies are.. and what the world looks like.

comments.author: Left-Excitement3829
comments.body: Neat ! I bet layer levels get bonkers

comments.author: gabro-games
comments.body: That game was awesome. I spent many happy hour playing it. Would love to see a web remake.

comments.author: nom-nom-babies
comments.body: I understand you are new to gamedev so just to let you know, for a project like this, you don’t need a game engine like godot. This would be much easier for whatever LLM you are using to build their own engine

replies.author: featherless_fiend
replies.body: No it could be argued that an LLM will have a much easier time dealing with tokens that represent more compressed information. Meaning the amount of lines of GDScript to code something requires much less lines than C++. So scripting languages are better for simple game development. In terms of less usage and more intelligence.

replies.author: nom-nom-babies
replies.body: Well as a person who’s done both, and to keep it short winded, I heavily disagree with you thinking it would be less tokens.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: sheesh who said it had to be c++ lol this could be a single file html+js

replies.author: Financial_Alps3369
replies.body: In that case we're looping back to using a game framework. With JS the LLM would probably utilize something like Phaser or another framework

replies.author: FrostyBuildsGames
replies.body: Sounds complicated 😄 Maybe it's not, thanks for the tip though! But I'm planning on releasing this on [itch.io](http://itch.io) and maybe later on mobile, and AI told me that Godot handles exporting to both. I'm also planning more maps, bosses and eventually a story.

replies.author: Financial_Alps3369
replies.body: There's countless reasons to use an established game engine. What if it gets popular and people want to mod it or add their own content? What if OP later wants to try his hand at implementing some content manually? Having that established base, especially for things like documentation, can be very valuable

replies.author: nom-nom-babies
replies.body: Everything you just said is easier if building your own engine. The fact you said c++ makes me think you aren’t actually a developer. The only reason for the op to use it for a project of his scope would be to learn how to use an established engine like Godot.

replies.author: Financial_Alps3369
replies.body:
I didn't mention anything about C++, so you might be referring to another comment. I am a developer, and using an engine like Godot does make collaboration easier precisely because most people are not seasoned developers.

Personally I do not use Godot or any game engine, but I do develop tooling for my game that makes it easier to add content mods. Using an engine would largely bypass the need for it

comments.author: axphin
comments.body: Looking good so far. I’ve only used JavaScript to prototype 2D or 3D games with Claude Code. But have been thinking about using Godot for some 3D stuff.

replies.author: FrostyBuildsGames
replies.body: Haha fair! It's simple now because I'm new and just starting to learn game dev 😄 The plan is my own enemies, maps and bosses later. Everyone starts somewhere.

replies.author: EthelUltima
replies.body:
Depends though if your trying to learn game dev  with aim to manually create games this is not the way. If you want to make a game with AI  and don't care how its made then there is no need to aim so low. Aim high and make it happen. There are people 1 prompting entire 3D playable games. 

People can downvote me all they want, but we should be doing awesome things with AI not just reinventing the wheel constantly.
